  N. Long-Term  Liabilities

  In the government-wide  financial  statements  and  proprietary  fund financial  statements,
  long-term  debt  and  other  long-term  obligations  are  reported  as liabilities  in the
  governmental  activities,  business-type  activities  or  proprietary  fund type statement  of net
  position. Bond premiums  and discounts  are deferred  and amortized  over the life of the bonds
  using the effective  interest  method.  Bonds payable  are reported  net of the applicable  bond
  premium  or discount.

  In the fund financial  statements,  governmental  fund types recognize  bond premiums  and
  discounts,  as well as bond issuance  costs, during  the current  period.  The face amount  of
  debt issued is reported  as other financing  sources.  Premiums  received  on debt issuances
  are reported  as other financing  sources  while discounts  on debt issuances  are reported  as
  other financing  uses.

  0, Net  Position

  In the governmental-wide  financial  statements  and  proprietary  fund  financial  statements,
  net position is classified  as follows:

  Net Investment  in Capital Assets - This amount  consists of capital assets net of accumulated
  depreciation  and reduced  by outstanding  debt and any deferred  outflows  or inflows  of
  resources  that are attributed  to the acquisition,  construction,  or improvement  of the assets,
  net of unspent  debt  proceeds  and deferred  gain/loss  on refunding  and retention  payable.

  Restricted  Net Position  - This  amount  is restricted  by  external  creditors,  grantors,
  contributors,  or laws or regulations  of other governments.

  Unrestricted  Net Position  - This component  of net position  is the amount  of the assets,
  deferred  outflows  of resources,  liabilities, and deferred  inflows  of resources  that are not
  included  in the determination  of net investment  in capital assets or the restricted  component
  of net position.

  Sometimes  the government  will fund outlays  for a particular  purpose  from both restricted
  (e.g., restricted  bond or grant proceeds)  and unrestricted  resources.  In order to calculate
  the amounts  to report  as restricted  - net position  and unrestricted  - net position  in the
  government-wide  and proprietary  fund financial  statements,  a flow assumption  must be
  made about  the order  in which  the resources  are considered  to be applied.  It is the
  government's  policy to consider  restricted  - net position  to have been depleted  before
  unrestricted  - net position  is applied.

  (b) legally or contractually  required  to be maintained  intact.

  Restricted  - This portion of a fund balance reflects constraints  placed on the use of resources
  (other than non-spendable  items) that are either:  (a) externally  imposed  by creditors  (such
  as through  debt  covenants),  grantors, contributors,  or laws or regulations  of other
  governments;  or (b)  imposed  by law through  constitutional  provisions  or enabling
  legislation.

  Committed  - This portion  of a fund balance  includes  amounts  that can only be used for
  specific  purposes  pursuant  to constrains  imposed  by formal  action  of the government's
  highest  level  of decision-making  authority  (City  Council),  and remain  binding  unless
  removed  in the same manner.  The City Council,  as the City's highest  level of decision-
  making  authority,  may commit  fund balance  for specific  purposes  pursuant  to constraints
  imposed  by the adoption  of a resolution.  These committed  amounts  cannot be used for any
  other purpose  unless the City Council  removes  or changes  the specified  use through  the
  same type of formal action taken to establish  the commitment.  As part of the City's initiative

  R. Changes  in Accounting  Policy

  During  fiscal  year  ended  June  30, 2022,  the  City  implemented  the  following  new  GASB
  Pronouncement  :

  GASB Statement  No. 87, Leases - The primary objective  of this Statement  is to meet the
  information  needs of financial  statement  users by improving  accounting  and financial
  reporting  of leases  by governments.  The Statement  increases  the usefulness  of
  governments  financial  statements  by requiring  recognition  of certain  lease assets and
  liabilities for leases that previously  were classified  as operating  leases and recognized  as
  inflow of resources  and outflow  of resources  based on the payment  provisions  of the
  contract.  It establishes  a single model for lease accounting  based on the foundational
  principle  that leases are financings  or' the right to use an underlying  asset.  Under this
  Statement,  a lessee is required to recognize a lease liability and an intangible  right to use
  lease asset, and a lessor is required to recognize a lease receivable  and a deferred inflow of
  resources,  thereby  enhancing  the  relevance  and consistency  of information  about
  governments  leasing activities.

  common  investment  and administrative  agent for participating  public entities within the State
  of California.  Benefit  provisions  and all other requirements  are established  by state statue
  and City ordinance.  A full description  of the pension  plan regarding  number  of employees
  covered,  benefit  provisions,  assumptions  (for funding,  but not accounting  purposes),  and
  membership  information  are listed in the annual  actuarial  valuation  report.  This report and

  Industrial  disability  benefits are not offered to miscellaneous  employees.  The City provides
  industrial  disability  retirement  benefit  to safety  employees.  The industrial  disability

  An employee's  beneficiary  may receive the basic death benefit if the employee  dies while
  actively employed.  The employee  must be actively employed with the City to be eligible for
  this benefit.  An employee's  survivor  who is eligible for any other pre-retirement  death
  benefit may choose to receive that death benefit instead of this basic death benefit. The
  basic death  benefit  is a lump  sum in the amount  of the employee's  accumulated
  contributions,  where interest is currently  credited at 6 percent per year, plus a lump sum in
  the amount  of one month's  salary for each completed  year of current  service,  up to a
  maximum  of six months' salary. For purposes of this benefit, one month's salary is defined
  as the member's  average  monthly  full-time  rate of compensation  during the 12 months
  preceding death.

  Upon the death of a retiree, a one-time lump,sum payment of $500 will be made to the
  retiree's  designated  survivor(s),  or to the retiree's  estate.

  Benefit terms provide for annual cost-of-living adjustments  to each employee's  retirement
  allowance.  Beginning the second calendar year after the year or retirement,  retirement  and
  survivor allowances will be annually adjusted on a compound  basis by 2 percent.

  costs of benefits earned by employees during the year, with an additional  amount to finance
  any unfunded  accrued  liability.  The employer  is required  to contribute  the difference
  between the actuarially  determined  rate and the contribution  rate of employees.  Employer
  contribution  rates may change :F plan contracts  are amended.  Payments  made by the

  Lonq-Term  Expected  Rate of Return

  The long-term  expected  rate of return on pension plan investments  was determined  using
  a building-block  method in which expected future real rates of return (expected  returns, net
  of pension plan investment  expense and inflation) are developed for each major asset class.

  In determining  the long-term  expected rate of return, CalPERS took into account both short-
  term and long-term  market return expectations  as well as the expected  pension fund cash
  flows.  Using  historical  returns  of all the funds'  asset classes,  expected  compound
  (geometric)  returns were calculated  over the short-term  (first 10 years) and the long-term
  (11+ years) using a building-block  approach.  Using the expected nominal returns for both
  short-term  and long-term,  the present value of benefits was calculated  for each fund. The
  expected rate of return was set by calculating  the rounded single equivalent  expected return
  that arrived at the same present value of benefits for cash flows as the one calculated  using
  both short-term  and long-term  returns. The expected  rate of return was then set equal to
  the single  equivalent  rate calculated  above  and adjusted  to account  for assumed
  administrative  expenses.

  On July 12, 2021, CalPERS reported  a preliminary  21.3'/o net return on investments  for
  fiscal year 2020-21.  Based on the thresholds  specified in CalPERS Funding Risk Mitigation
  policy, the excess return of 14.3'/o  prescribes  a reduction  in investment  volatility  that
  corresponds  to a reduction  in the discount rate used for funding purposes of O.20'/o,  from
  7.00o/o to 6.80o/o. Since CalPERS was in the final stages of the four-year  Asset Liability
  Management  (ALM) cycle, the board elected to defer any changes to the asset allocation
  until the ALM process concluded,  and the board could make its final decision on the asset
  allocation  in November  2021.

  On November 17, 2021, the board adopted a new strategic asset allocation.  The new asset
  allocation  along with the new capital  market  assumptions,  economic  assumptions  and
  administrative  expense assumption  support a discount  rate of 6.90'/o  (net of investment
  expense  but without  a reduction  for administrative  expense)  for financial  reporting

  as recommended  in the November  2021 CalPERS Experience Study and Review or Actuarial

  new assumptions  will be reflected in the GASB 68 accounting  valuation  reports for the June

  B. Supplemental  Retirement  Plan

  General  Information  about  the  Pension  Plan

  Plan Description

  Effective  July 1, 2002, the City established  a supplemental  retirement  plan with the Public
  Agency  Retirement  System  ("PARS").  The supplemental  retirement  plan administered  by
  PARS (the "PARS plan")  is an agent multiple-employer  defined  benefit  pension  plan. The
  PARS plan is separated  into two tiers. The PARS plan was organized  under the authority  of
  the City Council and may be amended  by the City Council.  The City issues a stand-alone
  financial  report that is available  to the public. The report is available  on the City's website.

  Benefits  Provided

  Tier one provides  for the difference  between  the 3'/o at 55 benefits  and the 2.7'/0  at 55
  benefits for years  of service to the City. Eligibility  to receive benefits  is as follows:

  *  Must be a full-time  Top Management  miscellaneous  (non-safety)  employee  of the
  City of South Gate on or after July 1, 2002.  Employees  hired after December  31,
  2012 are not eligible to participate in the Plan.
  *  Must have completed  three years of full-time  continuous  employment  with the City
  prior to retirement.
  *  Must concurrently  retire from PERS at the time of application  for benefits  under this
  plan.
  *  Must either 1) be at least fifty-five  years of age, if retirement  is concurrent  with
  separation  from the City or 2) be at least sixty years of age.
  *  Must apply for the benefits,  and meet the age requirements.

  Tier two provides  a monthly lifetime  annuity  payment  to eligible  employees  in lieu of post-
  employment  health care benefits.  Eligibility  to receive benefits  is as follows:

  *  Must  have retired from the City with 20 or more years of service.
  *  Must  remain  retired.
  *  Must  not participate  in the PERS health plan offered by the City.

  The City administers  a single-employer  defined-benefit  post-employment  healthcare  plan
  (the Plan). Dependents  are eligible  to enroll,  and benefits  continue  to surviving  spouses.

  remain in or enroll in a CalPERS plan upon retirement,  and remain  so retired.  For 2021, the
  City reimburses  retirees  who have attained  age 50 and at least 20 years of service for 100'/o
  of premiums up to a maximum of $150/month for NonSafety Employees, $200/month for
  Top Management Employees,  and $250/month for Safety Employees who retired before July
  1 , 2005. Safety employees  retired after July 1, 2005, who have attained  age 50 and at least
  2 0 years of service  are eligible  to receive  up to the two-party  Kaiser rate in effect on July
  1, 2005 and increased  each year by 5'/o maximum.  The maximum  does not change  based
  on Medicare  eligibility  or spouse coverage.  The terms  of benefits  provided  are authorized

  from  Safety National  Casualty  Corporation.  Under  this policy,  Safety  National  covers  all
  workers'  compensation  claim expenses over $1,000,000  per claim  for safety and over
  $750,000  for non-safety.  An Internal  Service  Fund is used to account  for the collection  of
  premiums  from various  City departments  related  to the amount  of workers'  compensation
  policy  premium  paid and general  claims  liabilities.  Premiums  assessed  for general  claim
  liabilities  are established  based on historical  claims experience.  The City is a member  of the

  provide  liability  insurance  coverage  for independent  cities. Under the terms of the agreement
  with the Authority,  the City is insured for losses above $250,000  per claim.

  On December 29, 2011, the California Supreme Court upheld Assembly Bill IX 26 ("the Bill")
  that provided for the dissolution of all redevelopment  agencies in the State of California.  This
  action impacted the reporting entity of the City of South Gate that previously had reported a
  redevelopment  agency within the reporting entity of the City as a blended component unit.
  The Bill provided that upon dissolution of a redevelopment  agency, either the City or another
  unit of local government  will agree to serve as the "successor agency" to hold the assets until
  they are distributed  to other units of state and local government.  On January 11, 2012,  the
  City Council elected to become the Successor Agency for the former redevelopment  agency  in
  accordance with the Bill as part of City resolution number  7473.

  State of California cannot enter into new projects, obligations or commitments.  Subject  to the

  housing project located within the boundaries  of the South Gate Community  Development
  Commission  at 8931 Dudlext Avenue consisting  of 20 senior 1-bedroom  units. South Gate
  Realty Group must comply with Housing and Urban Development  (HUD) rents for 30 years
  from the certificate  of occupancy date.

  year starting from the occupancy date if South Gate Realty Group can illustrate compliance
  with the Disposition and Development Agreement (DDA). The DDA limits the rent at $620
  per unit less $50 utility allowance for a net of $570 per month or less. The compliance
  report is required to be submitted to the City each month in order to receive the $51,222
  annual forgiveness. At June 30, 2022, the outstanding balance on the loan is $153,656.

Budgets  and  Budgetary  Accounting

The City adheres  to general  procedures  in establishing  its annual  budget,  which is reflected  in the
accompanying  budgetary  statements  and schedules.  The annual budget adopted  by the City Council
provides  for the general operations  of the City. It includes  proposed  expenditures  and the means  of
financing  them. Budgeted  appropriations  lapse at the end of the year. The City Council approves  total
budgeted  appropriations  and amendments  to appropriations  throughout  the year. The City Council must
approve budget transfers  between departments,  funds and activities,  as well as for the use of salary and
benefit appropriations  for something  other than salary and benefits. The departments  of the General Fund
are considered  to be departments  for purposes of this requirement.  Actual expenditures  may not legally
exceed budgeted appropriations  at the department  level. The level of budgetary  control (that is, the level
at which expenditures  cannot legally exceed the appropriated  amount at the department  level, which is
the legal level of control) is established  at the department  level within each fund.

Annual budgets are adopted for all Governmental  Funds on a basis substantially  consistent  with Generally
Accepted  Accounting  Principles  (GAAP). Formal budgetary  information  is employed  as a management
control  device. Commitments  for materials  and services,  such as purchase  orders and contracts  are
recorded during the year as encumbrances  to assist in controlling  expenditures.  All appropriationslapse
at year-end.  Encumbrances  for open purchase  orders and/or ongoing  projects  or contracts  are carried
over and are added to the followinq  year's budqeted appropriations.

Capital  Asset  & Equipment  Replacement  Fund  - To account  for the  Funding  and  replacement  of the

   CUSTODIAL  FUNDS

CUSTODIAL  FUNDS  accounts  for  assets  held  by  the  City  as  an  agent  for  individuals,  private
organizations,  other governments  and/or  other funds. Cash resources  are collected,  held for a brief  period
and then  distributed  to the  proper  recipients.  The City has a fiduciary  responsibility  for the assets,  which
it does  not own.  The following  funds  are classified  as an custodial  fund  in the financial  statements:

Tweedy  P &  BIA  - This  fund  is funded  for  several  eligible  events  and  activities  under  the  Tweedy
Parking  and  Business  Improvement  District  (BID).  To raise  funds,  each  business  in the  District  area  will
pay an assessment  along  with  the  City  Business  License.  Assessments  charged  to each  business  will vary
depending  on the gross  income  reported  on their License application/renewal.  Decision  regarding  use of
the BID funds are made  by an Advisory  Board appointed  by the City Council.

Special  Deposits  Fund  - This fund is used to account  for  deposits  placed  with  the  City  for  future
services  and trust  Funds awaiting remittance to relevant service  providers.

CITY OF SOUTH GATE
  REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MINUTES
  TUESDAY, JANUARY 24, 2023

CALL TO ORDER  Maria del Pilar Avalos, Mayor called a Regular City Council Meeting to
  order at 6:46 p.m.

INVOCATION  Tine Fierro, Deputy Director of Parks & Recreation

PLEDGE OF
ALLEGIANCE  Norma Cardenas Frank, newly promoted Senior Code Enforcement
  Officer
ROLL CALL  Debbie McEvilly, Recording Secretary

PRESENT  Mayor Maria del Pilar Avalos, Vice Mayor Gil Hurtado, Council Member
  Joshua Barron, Council Member Maria Davila, and Council Member Al
  Rios; City Treasurer Jose De La Paz, City Manager Chris Jeffers, City
  Attorney Raul F. Salina

1
PERSONNEL RECRUITMENT
& SELECTION  The City Council received and filed the list of new and promoted full-time
  employees hired or promoted during November and December 2022.

2
PERSONNEL BENEFITS/
RETIREMENT ADMIN  The City Council waived the reading in full and introduced Ordinance No.
  2023-01-CC entitled Ordinance of the City Council of the City of South
  Gate, California, authorizing an amendment to the contract between the
  City and the Board of Administration of the California Public Employees'
  Retirement System implementing Section 20516 (Employees Sharing
  Additional Cost) to provide employee cost sharing of 2% for classic local
  police members in the South Gate Police Management Association.

  Kristopher Ryan, Director of Administrative Services stated this is an
  introduction and first reading of an ordinance authorizing an amendment
  to the contract between the City and the California Public Employees'
  Retirement System (Ca1PERS). This would authorize an implementation
  for the cost sharing program. Both parties agreed to this during the most
  current labor negotiations.

  Mr. Ryan stated that the other labor groups, during labor negotiations also
  agreed to some types of cost sharing program.

  Mayor Avalos asked if anyone in the audience and zoom wished to speak
  on this item.

  Mario Dominguez, Jr., commented, "make them pay."
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF JANUARY 24, 2023

2
PERSONNEL BENEFITS/
RETIREMENT ADMIN
CONT'D  Having no one else come forward, Mayor Avalos closed the audience
  portion.

  Vice Mayor Hurtado moved to approve staff's recommendation and
  seconded by Mayor Avalos.

  ROLL CALL: Mayor Avalos, yes; Vice Mayor Hurtado, yes; Council
  Member Barron, yes; Council Member Davila, yes; Council Member Rios,
  yes.

3
PARKING & TRAFFIC  The City Council:

  a. Waived the reading in full and adopted Resolution No. 2023-02-
  CC entitled Resolution of the City Council of the City of South Gate,
  California, approving and establishing a Preferential Parking District
  on San Jose Avenue from Cherokee Avenue to Sequoia Drive to
  prohibit parking between the hours of 7:00 PM to 2:00 AM;

  b. Directed the Public Works Department to install parking restriction
  signage within 90 days of the approval of the Resolution;

  c. Directed the City Clerk to notify the property owners on San Jose of
  the January 24, 2023, voting results; and

  d. Appropriated $3,000 in Gas Tax Funds to install the parking
  restrictions.

  Arturo Cervantes, Director of Public Works introduced Mr. Isaac Bravo.
  Mr. Bravo is the Management Analyst for the Public Works
  Department/Engineering Division and is here to make the presentation.

  Mr. Bravo stated that this item is to consider establishing a preferential
  parking district on San Jose from Cherokee Avenue to Sequoia Drive.
  There are seven active districts within the city with different time frames.
  These preferential districts are allowed in the California Vehicle Code and
  in the city's municipal code.

  Mr. Bravo stated the residents voted on the established time from 7:00 PM
  to 2:00 AM. Each parcel will only be allowed two permits, per our
  municipal code.

  Mayor Avalos asked if anyone in the audience and zoom wished to speak
  on this item.

  Page 2 of 13
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF JANUARY 24, 2023
3
PARKING & TRAFFIC
CONT'D  Juan Martinez, 10246 San Jose Avenue thanked City Council for
  accepting their petition and helping the residents.

  Robert Avila, 10309 San Jose Avenue thanked City Council for accepting
  their petition and helping the residents.

  Mario Dominguez, Jr., stated he did not see any presentations.

  Having no one else come forward, Mayor Avalos closed the audience
  portion.

  Vice Mayor Hurtado motioned to move forward and seconded by Mayor
  Avalos.

  Council Member Barron stated living in a preferential parking district and
  recommends it to everyone.

  Council Member Davila, Council Member Rios and Mayor Avalos
  commend the residents on San Jose for uniting and requesting preferential
  parking.

  ROLL CALL: Mayor Avalos, yes; Vice Mayor Hurtado, yes; Council
  Member Barron, yes; Council Member Davila, yes; Council Member Rios,
  yes.

  Mayor Avalos thanked Public Works Department for having this
  procedure.

  City Attorney Salinas stated living at 10222 San Jose Avenue from 1967-
  1985.

COMMENTS FROM THE
AUDIENCE - NON-AGENDA
ITEMS  Reza Neamati, President of RN Development stated being in a financial
  difficulty due to the actions of Griffin Construction management team and
  the city management team since February 2022.

  Danielle of RN Development stated the city was forced to shut down the
  Urban Orchard Project. The project is eighty percent done. She also
  mentioned this is causing financial difficulty.

  Eddie Barker of RN Development stated this was to make the Council
  aware of the situation. RN Development is asking for the Council's help.

  George Duarte, owner, and founder of Roocket Fitness. They have been
  open for 10 years in different cities. He stated two years ago he has had
  issues with the city due to parking.

  Page 3 of 13
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF JANUARY 24, 2023

COMMENTS FROM THE
AUDIENCE - NON-AGENDA
ITEMS CONT'D  Lizette Ruiz, Kauffman Avenue spoke on pet and animal welfare. She has
  volunteered as part of the trap-neuter-return program coordinated by
  FixNation in Sun Valley. She is a cofounder of a local group called
  SELLA Trap-Neuter-Return feral cats in the Southeast LA area. Ms. Ruiz
  is asking Council to bring back programs. She knows there used to be a
  mobile spay clinic at the park.

  Employee of RN Development. He oversees transportation and reiterates
  financial difficulty.

  Kevin, employee of RN Development. He is a carpenter and reiterates
  financial difficulty.

  Milagros Diaz, 10001 Frontage Road, stated that many of the seniors at
  Thunderbird Villa were excited about the Urban Orchard Project. Ms.
  Diaz stated the seniors are now disappointed.

  Armando Velasquez, Independence Avenue hopes this project gets
  resolved. Mr. Velasquez thanked the city for having the Kiwanis Club at
  the Centennial celebration. He stated the club will be participating in the
  Homeless Count tomorrow. He invited everyone to the monthly Kiwanis
  cleanup on February 18th at the Willow Elementary School. They are
  launching two bingo nights for the senior citizens on February 3rd and
  February 23rd. A major event will be held at the South Gate auditorium on
  February 4th for all Kiwanis Clubs to elect district and state leaders.

  Frank Rivera, 9700 block of McNerney Avenue congratulated the
  residents on San Jose for establishing their preferential parking. Mr.
  Rivera reminded the city of the 2019 Parking Study. Mr. Rivera is
  requesting Council agendize an update report.

  Mario Dominguez, Jr., stated that if the city is not going to implement the
  parking study, then forget about it. Mr. Dominguez asked if the NR
  Development has to do with Item 8. He asked the city to finish the Urban
  Orchid Project.

  Jocelyn Panduro, Student Body Vice President at South Gate High School
  is requesting a donation of $2,000 for their All Student Body (ASB) class
  to purchase custom jerseys to wear at events to represent their ASB and
  school.

  Thomas Buckley stated that a resident that resides in Elizabeth and
  Southern is still waiting for an update on the street light issues. Another
  complaint is about UWS and prefers Waste Management. Mr. Buckley
  stated that on January 21st was a murder that happened in bright daylight

  Page 4 of 13
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF JANUARY 24, 2023

COMMENTS FROM THE
AUDIENCE - NON-AGENDA
ITEMS CONT'D  on State and Illinois. Mr. Buckley thanked South Gate PD and Sheriff's
  for investigating and hopes the suspect or suspects will be captured.

  Cyndi Esquivel thanked the city and committee that oversaw putting
  together the Centennial celebration.

  Jacqueline attended last month's Council Meeting and is asking for status
  if the city has informed the community of vehicle thefts.

REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS  Chris Jeffers, City Manager stated for the student that called in for the
  ASB donation. He is asking the student to call the Chief and make an
  application to the Youth Commission for funding. His response to Mr.
  Rivera regarding the 2019 Park Study. The item was not presented to the
  Council until 2021. There were over 180 recommendations with different
  criteria to implement.

  Arturo Cervantes, Director of Public Works stated that there are several
  lighting outages impacting the city. He mentioned circuit 37 as an example
  is a Southern California Edison issue.

  Mr. Jeffers to Ms. Ruiz staff will look at the mobile clinic and provide
  Council with an update on that process. To Mr. Duarte that was one of the
  areas that Council took affirmative action to reduce parking requirements.

  Mr. Jeffers stated that the Council is aware the county issued a stop notice
  on the Orchard Urban Project until the city obtains a notice called a
  closure permit. It is impacting the contractor and the city. The Council will
  be having a special meeting in a week or two for a thorough report on this
  project. Mr. Jeffers told everyone that the project will get done.

  Chief Arakawa stated that the investigation is ongoing. The police
  department is working with the Los Angeles Sheriff's Department on the
  incident that happened on January 21'.

  Arturo Cervantes, Director of Public Works announced that the public
  works department is getting ready to start the fire hydrant flushing
  maintenance program. It begins on January 29th' and it will take four
  months to complete.

  Tina Fierro, Deputy Director of Parks & Recreation gave a recap on the
  Centennial event.

  Meredith Elguira, Director of Community Development stated that the
  rental assistance program started today. A community meeting was held
  with regards to the Draft EIR for the Patata Project.

  Page 5 of 13
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF JANUARY 24, 2023
REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS
CONT'D  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk thanked all the city employees, volunteers,
  vendors, and performers that were present at Saturday's event.

  Jose De La Paz, City Treasurer stated the community would like to know
  the city's stand on streets vendors. The second item is a timeline on the
  Tweedy Boulevard resurfacing and when it will occur. The third item is
  for the Council to place an item on the agenda adding cameras to our
  chambers for future Council meetings. Lastly, he will attend the bingo and
  the next clean-up.

  Kris Ryan, Director of Administrative Services provided information to
  the public and residents on the UWS and how they are going to start
  housing in city hall to assist customers with any issues.

  Jon Hamilton, Director of Human Resources enjoyed the Centennial
  event. Mr. Hamilton stated new jobs flyers are posted regularly on the
  city's website.

  Chief of Arakawa reported ten (10) police explorers participated at the 25th
  Annual Chandler, Arizona tactical competition. He also stated the police
  department are in the infantile stages of planning the next citizen academy
  which will take place in March.

  Chris Jeffers, City Manager extended his gratitude to the employees and
  departments that participated in the Centennial event. Also, to the
  committee that helped organize the event. Mr. Jeffers stated it will be a
  full year of activities and ending with the reburying of the time capsule
  next January. The staff is diligently working to present the items that were
  inside the time capsule to the public. Mr. Jeffers stated Giselle is currently
  working on the City's E-Newsletter for residents to sign up and get the
  latest news.

  Mr. Jeffers asked Mr. Cervantes if he would speak on the Tweedy Mile
  resurfacing.

  Mr. Cervantes stated that the schedule is currently under design. It will
  probably be completed in the next four or five months. The project is
  federally funded. The outreach is forthcoming in the next month or so.

  Mr. Jeffers mentioned that street vendors are allowed in certain areas
  because state law requires it under certain conditions.

  Council Member Davila stated that it has been an honor being on Council
  during the Centennial. Everyone that attended the event had a great time.
  She thanked the committee, employees, vendors, agencies, and
  clubs/organizations for participating. Virginia Johnson will be missed.

  Page 6 of 13
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF JANUARY 24, 2023
REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS
CONT'D  Council Member Barron stated the Centennial was a great event. He
  thanked the committee and Parks Department for their hard work. He also
  thanked the clubs/organizations for their participation.

  Council Member Barron attended the ICA meeting on January 12th and
  met Mrs. Davenport CEO of Los Angeles County. She provided
  information about what the county is trying to do to aid the homeless.

  Council Member Barron stated that he has the South Gate Police
  Departments app on his phone and asked Chief Arakawa to speak on it.

  Chief Arakawa encourages everyone to be active and be a neighborhood
  watch captain. We can have information on the social media pages and on
  the app.

  Mr. Jeffers mentioned the Chief will be presenting the annual crime
  statistics.

  Council Member Barron understands the police department must be
  careful what information is available on the app because criminals can
  have that app too.

  Council Member Rios stated the Centennial was a great event. He thanked
  the committee and everyone that participated. He is looking forward to the
  other activities during the year.

  Council Member Rios assured NR Development and the others that were
  impacted that we care deeply about this project, and we want to resolve it.

  Council Member Rios mentioned the spring semester is starting at ELAC.

  Vice Mayor Hurtado doesn't understand when the mass shooting will be
  under control. He reached out to the congresswoman's staff asking for
  help regarding street light issues. He also reached out to State Senator
  Lena Gonzalez and Assembly Member Anthony Rendon.

  Vice Mayor Hurtado stated the Centennial was a great event.

  Mayor Avalos thanked the departments and community for celebrating the
  city's Centennial. She thanked her colleagues for giving her the
  opportunity to be the mayor for the 100th celebration.

  Mayor Avalos attended the LA Sanitation meeting and the new directors
  in March to enlighten us as to what exactly is that they do. She also
  attended the HUB Cities meeting and they reviewed their annual budget.

  Page 7 of 13
